passages.title: Passage I (Questions 11–15)
passages.body: As to happiness, I am not so sure. Birds, it is true, die of hunger in large numbers during the winter, if they are not birds of passage. But during the summer they do not foresee this catastrophe, or remember how nearly it befell them in the previous winter. With human beings the matter is otherwise. I doubt whether the percentage of birds that will have died of hunger during the present winter (1946-47) is as great as the percentage of human beings that will have died from this cause in India and central Europe during the same period. But every human death by starvation is preceded by a long period of anxiety, and surrounded by the corresponding anxiety of neighbours. We suffer not only the evils that actually befall us, but all those that our intelligence tells us we have reason to fear. The curbing of impulses to which we are led by forethought averts physical disaster at the cost of worry, and general lack of joy. I do not think that the learned men of my acquaintance, even when they enjoy a secure income, are as happy as the mice that eat the crumbs from their tables while the erudite gentlemen snooze. In this respect, therefore, I am not convinced that there has been any progress at all.
passages.source: CDS II 2021 English set A (set code NYRG-F-ENG – A)

passages.title: Passage II (Questions 16–20)
passages.body:
More than eight months after the national lockdown was announced in late March, urban India is learning to live with the Covid-19 pandemic. In fact, indicating a positive outlook for the future, many survey respondents in a recent survey say they plan to return to pre-lockdown levels of shopping, personal grooming, going to cinemas and socializing as pandemic fears continues to recede.

The survey findings highlight that the suppression of consumer demand because of fears of job losses and salary cuts could be coming to an end. Increasingly, urban Indians are showing increased confidence about the future of the economy. This could be an indicator of the possible ‘pent-up demand’ that several economists have been talking about — a demand that could be unleashed once a vaccine is developed and distributed, or when there are signs of the pandemic’s spread reducing to negligible levels or vanishing totally.

Around 65 per cent of respondents said they had settled into new routines, or that they saw signs of the situation improving, or they had come to terms with the pandemic and were moving on with their lives. And since the survey was conducted before the news of the successful trials of the Pfizer vaccine for the coronavirus was announced, it is likely that the consumers are now even more positive in their outlook about the future.
passages.source: CDS II 2021 English set A (set code NYRG-F-ENG – A)

passages.title: Cloze passage (Questions 101–110)
passages.body: The polythene bags (101) _____ non-biodegradable, i.e., they cannot be decomposed (102) _____ micro-organisms into manure. They remain as (103) _____ even after years. Animals that started eating waste food (104) _____ with these polythene bags, ultimately started dying (105) _____ their internal system was getting blocked. The Government had no alternative (106) _____ to ban these polythene bags. It is (107) _____ duty of the Government to look into this matter; however, it is also the duty of each individual to (108) _____ that we (109) _____ use polythene bags. By using these we will not only harm the environment but ourselves as well. Thus, say ‘No’ to plastic bags and contribute (110) _____ society.
passages.source: CDS II 2021 English set A (set code NYRG-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the option that best completes the sentence.

I asked two people the way to the station ______
questions.opt_a: but neither of them could help me
questions.opt_b: however none of them could show me the way
questions.opt_c: yet they had doubts about the station
questions.explanation:
Concept: Complete the sentence logically and grammatically.
Step 1: 'But' links the two clauses with a contrast: I asked, but neither could help.
Step 2: 'However' and 'nevertheless' are adverbs, not conjunctions, so they cannot join the clauses without a full stop or semicolon.
Answer: (a).
questions.source: CDS II 2021 English set A (set code NYRG-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the option that best completes the sentence.

The room was very warm ______
questions.opt_a: because the AC was set to moderate temperature
questions.opt_b: though the AC was set to very cold
questions.opt_c: since the AC was not very warm in its temperature setting
questions.opt_d: since the AC was in a very low temperature setting
questions.explanation:
Concept: Complete the sentence logically and grammatically.
Step 1: UPSC's key is (a): the room was warm because the AC was set only to a moderate temperature.
Step 2: (b) 'though the AC was set to very cold' also reads naturally, so treat this item as low-confidence.
Answer: (a).
questions.source: CDS II 2021 English set A (set code NYRG-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the option that best completes the sentence.

We could leave today or we could leave tomorrow ______
questions.opt_b: as you prefer one of the two
questions.explanation:
Concept: Complete the sentence logically and grammatically.
Step 1: 'Depending on what you prefer' says the choice rests with the listener.
Step 2: The other options are awkward or ungrammatical in this position.
Answer: (c).
questions.source: CDS II 2021 English set A (set code NYRG-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the option that best completes the sentence.

Mohan and I couldn’t get into the house because ______
questions.opt_a: neither of us had the keys
questions.opt_b: both of us do not have the keys
questions.opt_c: either of us did not have the keys
questions.opt_d: neither of us did have the keys
questions.explanation:
Concept: Complete the sentence logically and grammatically.
Step 1: 'Neither of us had the keys' keeps the past tense and the negative meaning.
Step 2: (b) is present tense, (c) is illogical, and (d) is clumsy.
Answer: (a).
questions.source: CDS II 2021 English set A (set code NYRG-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the option that best completes the sentence.

There are many good hotels, you can choose to stay in ______
questions.explanation:
Concept: Complete the sentence logically and grammatically.
Step 1: Choosing one hotel among many takes 'any one of them'.
Step 2: 'Either' is for two, and you cannot stay in all of them.
Answer: (b).
questions.source: CDS II 2021 English set A (set code NYRG-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the option that best completes the sentence.

The bus service is very good; there is a bus ______
questions.explanation:
Concept: Complete the sentence logically and grammatically.
Step 1: A good service means a bus comes at regular intervals: 'every ten minutes'.
Answer: (d).
questions.source: CDS II 2021 English set A (set code NYRG-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the option that best completes the sentence.

We live near a busy airport; the planes fly ______
questions.explanation:
Concept: Complete the sentence logically and grammatically.
Step 1: Planes pass above the house, so 'over our house'.
Answer: (c).
questions.source: CDS II 2021 English set A (set code NYRG-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the option that best completes the sentence.

Dan was very quiet. He didn’t say a word ______
questions.explanation:
Concept: Complete the sentence logically and grammatically.
Step 1: 'The entire evening' is the correct phrase.
Step 2: 'All the evening' is less idiomatic, 'all the entire' is redundant, and 'entire evening' lacks an article.
Answer: (b).
questions.source: CDS II 2021 English set A (set code NYRG-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the option that best completes the sentence.

I don’t like stories ______
questions.explanation:
Concept: Complete the sentence logically and grammatically.
Step 1: 'Stories that have unhappy endings' is a natural defining clause in the present tense.
Answer: (c).
questions.source: CDS II 2021 English set A (set code NYRG-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the option that best completes the sentence.

Not everything ______
questions.explanation:
Concept: Complete the sentence logically and grammatically.
Step 1: After 'everything', the relative pronoun is 'that': 'Not everything that happened was my fault'.
Step 2: 'Which happen' mismatches the verb, and 'what' and 'whatever' do not follow 'everything'.
Answer: (a).
questions.source: CDS II 2021 English set A (set code NYRG-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Reading Comprehension
questions.question: The birds die of hunger in winter because
questions.opt_a: they do not move to warmer places
questions.opt_c: they do not get the food of their choice
questions.opt_d: they are too young to get the food
questions.explanation:
Concept: Use only what the passage says.
Step 1: The passage says birds die of hunger in winter 'if they are not birds of passage', that is, if they do not migrate.
Step 2: So the cause is that they do not move to warmer places.
Answer: (a).
questions.source: CDS II 2021 English set A (set code NYRG-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Reading Comprehension
questions.question: The birds do not foresee the catastrophe because they
questions.explanation:
Concept: Use only what the passage says.
Step 1: The passage says birds in summer 'do not foresee this catastrophe', unlike humans who worry in advance.
Step 2: UPSC's key is (c). (a) is close, so treat this item as low-confidence.
Answer: (c).
questions.source: CDS II 2021 English set A (set code NYRG-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Reading Comprehension
questions.question: Human beings cannot be happy because they
questions.opt_a: do not get time to enjoy
questions.opt_b: worry too much about their work
questions.explanation:
Concept: Use only what the passage says.
Step 1: The passage says we suffer the evils 'our intelligence tells us we have reason to fear', and forethought costs 'worry, and general lack of joy'.
Step 2: So humans worry too much about the future.
Answer: (d).
questions.source: CDS II 2021 English set A (set code NYRG-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Reading Comprehension
questions.question: Which one of the following is the antonym of the word ‘erudite’ in the passage?
questions.explanation:
Concept: Use only what the passage says.
Step 1: 'Erudite' means very learned. The opposite is 'ill-educated'.
Step 2: 'Learned' and 'qualified' are close in meaning.
Answer: (b).
questions.source: CDS II 2021 English set A (set code NYRG-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Reading Comprehension
questions.question: Which one of the following is the central theme of the passage?
questions.opt_a: Life of the birds and the mice
questions.opt_b: Starvation in India and central Europe
questions.explanation:
Concept: Use only what the passage says.
Step 1: The passage compares birds and humans to test happiness, and ends 'I am not convinced that there has been any progress at all'.
Step 2: The central theme is therefore the progress of mankind. The birds, mice and starvation are only examples.
Answer: (c).
questions.source: CDS II 2021 English set A (set code NYRG-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Reading Comprehension
questions.question: The general tone of the passage is that of
questions.explanation:
Concept: Use only what the passage says.
Step 1: The passage speaks of 'a positive outlook', people moving on, and consumers being 'even more positive'.
Step 2: The tone is optimism.
Answer: (a).
questions.source: CDS II 2021 English set A (set code NYRG-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Reading Comprehension
questions.question: The willingness of consumers to go back to normal lifestyle indicates their
questions.explanation:
Concept: Use only what the passage says.
Step 1: The passage links returning to normal spending with 'increased confidence about the future of the economy'.
Step 2: That shows a sense of economic security.
Answer: (d).
questions.source: CDS II 2021 English set A (set code NYRG-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Reading Comprehension
questions.question: Which statement in the passage/phrase indicates that ‘Life must go on’?
questions.opt_a: They settled into their new routines
questions.opt_b: Salary cuts could be coming to an end
questions.opt_c: People are moving on with their lives
questions.explanation:
Concept: Use only what the passage says.
Step 1: 'Moving on with their lives' is the phrase closest to 'life must go on'.
Step 2: Settling into routines is about adapting, not about continuing life as before.
Answer: (c).
questions.source: CDS II 2021 English set A (set code NYRG-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Reading Comprehension
questions.question: What does the author mean by ‘pent-up demand’?
questions.opt_a: Desire (suppressed) to spend money once pandemic is controlled
questions.opt_d: Criticism of the public on the pay-cuts
questions.explanation:
Concept: Use only what the passage says.
Step 1: The passage describes it as demand that 'could be unleashed once a vaccine is developed'.
Step 2: So it means suppressed desire to spend.
Answer: (a).
questions.source: CDS II 2021 English set A (set code NYRG-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Reading Comprehension
questions.question: What, according to the author, is the reason behind suppression of consumer demands?
questions.opt_a: The lack of vaccine till date
questions.opt_c: Motive to save up some money
questions.opt_d: Careful and calculative attitude of the general public
questions.explanation:
Concept: Use only what the passage says.
Step 1: The passage says demand was suppressed 'because of fears of job losses and salary cuts'.
Step 2: That is professional insecurity.
Answer: (b).
questions.source: CDS II 2021 English set A (set code NYRG-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Find the part of the sentence that has an error. If there is no error, choose (d).

__Everything is going well;__ (a) __we didn’t have__ (b) __any problem.__ (c) No error. (d)
questions.explanation:
Concept: Spot the grammatical error.
Step 1: The first clause is in the present, so the second needs the present perfect: 'we haven't had any problem'.
Step 2: 'Didn't have' in part (b) is wrong.
Answer: (b).
questions.source: CDS II 2021 English set A (set code NYRG-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Find the part of the sentence that has an error. If there is no error, choose (d).

__Lavanya hasn’t gone__ (a) __to work__ (b) __yesterday.__ (c) No error. (d)
questions.explanation:
Concept: Spot the grammatical error.
Step 1: 'Yesterday' is a finished time, so the simple past is needed: 'didn't go'.
Step 2: The present perfect in part (a) is wrong.
Answer: (a).
questions.source: CDS II 2021 English set A (set code NYRG-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Find the part of the sentence that has an error. If there is no error, choose (d).

__Look! The boy over there__ (a) __wears the same sweater__ (b) __as you.__ (c) No error. (d)
questions.explanation:
Concept: Spot the grammatical error.
Step 1: 'Look!' points to what is happening now, so use the present continuous: 'is wearing'.
Step 2: 'Wears' in part (b) is wrong.
Answer: (b).
questions.source: CDS II 2021 English set A (set code NYRG-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Find the part of the sentence that has an error. If there is no error, choose (d).

__It begins__ (a) __to turn dark:__ (b) __shall I switch on the lights?__ (c) No error. (d)
questions.explanation:
Concept: Spot the grammatical error.
Step 1: A change happening now takes the continuous form: 'It's beginning to turn dark'.
Step 2: Part (a) is wrong.
Answer: (a).
questions.source: CDS II 2021 English set A (set code NYRG-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Find the part of the sentence that has an error. If there is no error, choose (d).

__Raman and Mitali__ (a) __have been married__ (b) __for twenty years.__ (c) No error. (d)
questions.explanation:
Concept: Spot the grammatical error.
Step 1: 'Have been married for twenty years' is correct: present perfect with 'for'.
Step 2: There is no error.
Answer: (d).
questions.source: CDS II 2021 English set A (set code NYRG-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Find the part of the sentence that has an error. If there is no error, choose (d).

__I have played__ (a) __basketball__ (b) __for the past three hours.__ (c) No error. (d)
questions.explanation:
Concept: Spot the grammatical error.
Step 1: An activity that has gone on for three hours up to now takes the continuous form: 'I have been playing'.
Step 2: Part (a) is wrong.
Answer: (a).
questions.source: CDS II 2021 English set A (set code NYRG-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Find the part of the sentence that has an error. If there is no error, choose (d).

__Jamila had a book__ (a) __in front of her,__ (b) __but she didn’t read it.__ (c) No error. (d)
questions.explanation:
Concept: Spot the grammatical error.
Step 1: The book was in front of her at that time, so the action 'not reading' should be in the past continuous: 'she wasn't reading it'.
Step 2: Part (c) is the marked answer in the key. Treat this item as low-confidence, since 'didn't read' is also grammatical.
Answer: (c).
questions.source: CDS II 2021 English set A (set code NYRG-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Find the part of the sentence that has an error. If there is no error, choose (d).

__When she heard the news__ (a) __she hasn’t been__ (b) __very pleased.__ (c) No error. (d)
questions.explanation:
Concept: Spot the grammatical error.
Step 1: 'When she heard' is past, so the main clause must be past: 'she wasn't very pleased'.
Step 2: Part (b) is wrong.
Answer: (b).
questions.source: CDS II 2021 English set A (set code NYRG-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Find the part of the sentence that has an error. If there is no error, choose (d).

__Where are you coming from?__ (a) __Are you__ (b) __an American?__ (c) No error. (d)
questions.explanation:
Concept: Spot the grammatical error.
Step 1: Asking about origin uses the simple present: 'Where do you come from?'.
Step 2: Part (a) is wrong.
Answer: (a).
questions.source: CDS II 2021 English set A (set code NYRG-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Find the part of the sentence that has an error. If there is no error, choose (d).

__I went to Canada__ (a) __a few years ago__ (b) __for a holiday.__ (c) No error. (d)
questions.explanation:
Concept: Spot the grammatical error.
Step 1: 'I went to Canada a few years ago for a holiday' is correct.
Step 2: There is no error.
Answer: (d).
questions.source: CDS II 2021 English set A (set code NYRG-F-ENG – A)

questions.opt_a: The highest marking on a tree or a building
questions.opt_b: Person or organization that attracts only the top
questions.explanation:
Concept: Idiom.
Step 1: 'Top-notch' means of the highest quality.
Answer: (c).

questions.subject: Vocabulary
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the most appropriate meaning of the idiom or phrase.

Under the table
questions.explanation:
Concept: Idiom.
Step 1: 'Under the table' means done secretly, especially payments.
Answer: (d).
questions.source: CDS II 2021 English set A (set code NYRG-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Vocabulary
questions.theme: At the drop of a hat
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the most appropriate meaning of the idiom or phrase.

At the drop of a hat
questions.opt_a: Clumsy person who drops hats everywhere
questions.explanation:
Concept: Idiom.
Step 1: 'At the drop of a hat' means immediately, with little hesitation.
Answer: (b).
questions.source: CDS II 2021 English set A (set code NYRG-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Sentence Organisation
questions.topic: Ordering of Sentences in a Passage
questions.question:
Directions: S1 and S6 are fixed. Arrange P, Q, R and S in between so that the six sentences form a coherent passage.

S1: An ideal citizen is one who establishes his standard in everything.
S6: He can be called a thorough gentleman.
P: Because he is a true patriot.
Q: Also, he can lay down his life for the honour of his country.
R: That he can make any sacrifice for his motherland.
S: He loves his country so much so.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Find the opening idea, then follow the links (this, also, however).
Step 1: S ('He loves his country so much so') follows S1, and R ('That he can make any sacrifice') completes the 'so much so ... that' pattern.
Step 2: Q adds ('Also') the extreme sacrifice, and P ends with the reason 'Because he is a true patriot'.
Answer: (a) SRQP.
questions.source: CDS II 2021 English set A (set code NYRG-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Sentence Organisation
questions.topic: Ordering of Sentences in a Passage
questions.question:
Directions: S1 and S6 are fixed. Arrange P, Q, R and S in between so that the six sentences form a coherent passage.

S1: There are multiple legal avenues for patients to indict doctors, but rarely is it the other way round.
S6: It is clear that patients have multiple avenues to pursue, should they feel an injustice has been perpetrated against them.
P: An FIR can be lodged against them under the section 304A of the Indian Penal Code.
Q: A compensation case can be filed in a consumer forum.
R: For one occurrence, there are multiple forums where doctors have to defend themselves.
S: For instance, a complaint can be made to their employer.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Find the opening idea, then follow the links (this, also, however).
Step 1: R opens with the general point about multiple forums for doctors.
Step 2: S, Q and P give three examples ('For instance' leads), in the order complaint, compensation case, FIR.
Answer: (c) RSQP.
questions.source: CDS II 2021 English set A (set code NYRG-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Sentence Organisation
questions.topic: Ordering of Sentences in a Passage
questions.question:
Directions: S1 and S6 are fixed. Arrange P, Q, R and S in between so that the six sentences form a coherent passage.

S1: Paragraphs are the building blocks of any write-up.
S6: Understanding of these makes one a good writer of paragraphs.
P: A paragraph need not be pages together in length.
Q: But actually a paragraph is a group of at least five sentences on the lower limit.
R: In reality, unity and coherence, not length, constitute a real good paragraph.
S: Many people define paragraphs in terms of their length.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Find the opening idea, then follow the links (this, also, however).
Step 1: S states the common view that paragraphs are defined by length.
Step 2: Q gives the lower limit, P says it need not be pages long, and R ('In reality') gives the true test before S6.
Answer: (c) SQPR.
questions.source: CDS II 2021 English set A (set code NYRG-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Sentence Organisation
questions.topic: Ordering of Sentences in a Passage
questions.question:
Directions: S1 and S6 are fixed. Arrange P, Q, R and S in between so that the six sentences form a coherent passage.

S1: Then what is necessary with regard to taming science and technology is:
S6: Then why do we not tame atomic energy to peaceful purposes?
P: We must have the basic knowledge of the two.
Q: It is said, ‘Science is a useful servant but destructive master’.
R: By the misuse of science, mankind will meet its doom quite soon.
S: If we do not harness it for the welfare of mankind, I am afraid, a total annihilation is a must.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Find the opening idea, then follow the links (this, also, however).
Step 1: P completes S1 ('is: We must have the basic knowledge of the two').
Step 2: Q gives the saying about servant and master, S says what happens if we do not harness it, and R states the doom, leading to S6.
Answer: (b) PQSR.
questions.source: CDS II 2021 English set A (set code NYRG-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Sentence Organisation
questions.topic: Ordering of Sentences in a Passage
questions.question:
Directions: S1 and S6 are fixed. Arrange P, Q, R and S in between so that the six sentences form a coherent passage.

S1: Uttarakhand is vulnerable to disasters.
S6: The lack of ability to learn lessons from disasters, and the lack of any accountability, ensure the perpetuation of the situation.
P: The absence of necessary monitoring, early warning systems and the overall disaster management system add another layer of damages during the disasters.
Q: Major interventions act as force multipliers during such disasters.
R: The violation of legal and other prudent norms, further increases the damages.
S: Climate change is increasing these vulnerabilities.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Find the opening idea, then follow the links (this, also, however).
Step 1: S ('Climate change is increasing these vulnerabilities') follows S1, and Q adds that major interventions make disasters worse.
Step 2: R ('further increases') builds on Q, and P adds another layer of damage before S6.
Answer: (a) SQRP.
questions.source: CDS II 2021 English set A (set code NYRG-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Sentence Organisation
questions.topic: Ordering of Sentences in a Passage
questions.question:
Directions: S1 and S6 are fixed. Arrange P, Q, R and S in between so that the six sentences form a coherent passage.

S1: Now only fifteen minutes were left.
S6: Our performance was excellent.
P: Thank God, we rubbed the word ‘defeat’ writ large on our forehead.
Q: It was a game of life and death.
R: Each one had concluded that we were going to lose.
S: It was a matter of minutes.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Find the opening idea, then follow the links (this, also, however).
Step 1: R says everyone thought we would lose, and S says it was a matter of minutes.
Step 2: Q calls it a game of life and death, and P ('Thank God') gives the relief just before S6.
Answer: (d) RSQP.
questions.source: CDS II 2021 English set A (set code NYRG-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Sentence Organisation
questions.topic: Ordering of Sentences in a Passage
questions.question:
Directions: S1 and S6 are fixed. Arrange P, Q, R and S in between so that the six sentences form a coherent passage.

S1: The river Ganga is very important for us culturally, spiritually, ecologically as well as economically.
S6: Journey in the right direction is firmly making progress, gathering momentum and becoming a people’s movement.
P: It is rich in cultural heritage, natural splendour and biodiversity.
Q: People have used its water since the beginning of civilisation for different purposes.
R: It has most dense cultivation in its basin and is critical for ensuring food and water security.
S: We need to utilise its water for different purposes while ensuring that its natural ecology is protected, aquatic life thrives, and forests along the river remain rejuvenated.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Find the opening idea, then follow the links (this, also, however).
Step 1: P describes the river's heritage after S1, and R adds its cultivation and food security.
Step 2: Q says people have used its water since civilisation began, and S says how to use it now, leading to S6.
Answer: (d) PRQS.
questions.source: CDS II 2021 English set A (set code NYRG-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Sentence Organisation
questions.topic: Ordering of Sentences in a Passage
questions.question:
Directions: S1 and S6 are fixed. Arrange P, Q, R and S in between so that the six sentences form a coherent passage.

S1: The Republic Day in India falls on 26th January.
S6: He attends the march past.
P: The President of India takes the salute.
Q: It is organized at the India Gate.
R: People from far and wide come to witness it.
S: It is celebrated with great pomp and show.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Find the opening idea, then follow the links (this, also, however).
Step 1: S ('It is celebrated with great pomp and show') follows S1, and R says people come to witness it.
Step 2: Q gives the venue, and P names the President who takes the salute. S6 'He attends the march past' refers to him.
Answer: (c) SRQP.
questions.source: CDS II 2021 English set A (set code NYRG-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Sentence Organisation
questions.topic: Ordering of Sentences in a Passage
questions.question:
Directions: S1 and S6 are fixed. Arrange P, Q, R and S in between so that the six sentences form a coherent passage.

S1: Different people have different hobbies.
S6: Thus, they say, as many people, so many hobbies.
P: With hobbies, you spend time in a gainful way.
Q: In due course, that becomes your hobby.
R: Whatever leisure time you get, you use that in creative activity.
S: Hobby is a leisure time activity.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Find the opening idea, then follow the links (this, also, however).
Step 1: S defines a hobby as a leisure time activity, and R says leisure time is used creatively.
Step 2: Q says that in due course this becomes a hobby, and P adds the benefit before S6 'Thus ...'.
Answer: (c) SRQP.
questions.source: CDS II 2021 English set A (set code NYRG-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Sentence Organisation
questions.topic: Ordering of Sentences in a Passage
questions.question:
Directions: S1 and S6 are fixed. Arrange P, Q, R and S in between so that the six sentences form a coherent passage.

S1: Life in a village is ideal.
S6: They can no longer be considered backward.
P: Our villages are no longer dirty.
Q: Moreover, they are disease-free.
R: Because, the village people are well-educated now.
S: Rather, they are highly clean and tidy.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Find the opening idea, then follow the links (this, also, however).
Step 1: P says villages are no longer dirty, and S ('Rather') says they are clean and tidy.
Step 2: Q ('Moreover') adds that they are disease-free, and R gives the reason, leading to S6.
Answer: (b) PSQR.
questions.source: CDS II 2021 English set A (set code NYRG-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the most appropriate word or group of words for the blank.

Honesty is ______ on his face.
questions.explanation:

Step 1: 'Is written on his face' uses the past participle in the passive.
Answer: (b).
questions.source: CDS II 2021 English set A (set code NYRG-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the most appropriate word or group of words for the blank.

He lives ______ his pen.
questions.explanation:

Step 1: 'Live by his pen' means earn a living through writing.
Answer: (a).
questions.source: CDS II 2021 English set A (set code NYRG-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the most appropriate word or group of words for the blank.

Much water has run ______ the bridge since then.
questions.explanation:

Step 1: 'Much water has run under the bridge' is the fixed expression for time passed.
Answer: (c).
questions.source: CDS II 2021 English set A (set code NYRG-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:

The gun ______ with a loud noise.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Choose the word that fits grammar and meaning.
Step 1: A gun 'goes off' when it fires.
Answer: (b).
questions.source: CDS II 2021 English set A (set code NYRG-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the most appropriate word or group of words for the blank.

They fought ______ the last man in the army.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Choose the word that fits grammar and meaning.
Step 1: 'Fight to the last man' means to fight until no one remains.
Answer: (d).
questions.source: CDS II 2021 English set A (set code NYRG-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:

Keep him ______ arm’s length.

Concept: Choose the word that fits grammar and meaning.
Step 1: 'At arm's length' means at a distance.
Answer: (a).
questions.source: CDS II 2021 English set A (set code NYRG-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the most appropriate word or group of words for the blank.

He succeeded ______.

Concept: Choose the word that fits grammar and meaning.
Step 1: 'In the long run' means eventually.

Answer: (c).
questions.source: CDS II 2021 English set A (set code NYRG-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the most appropriate word or group of words for the blank.

Have you ever tried ______ a coconut tree?
questions.explanation:
Concept: Choose the word that fits grammar and meaning.
Step 1: 'Tried climbing' means tested the activity.
Step 2: 'Going up' is also possible, but UPSC's key is 'climbing'.
Answer: (a).
questions.source: CDS II 2021 English set A (set code NYRG-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:

He is a man ______ means.

Concept: Choose the word that fits grammar and meaning.

Answer: (c).
questions.source: CDS II 2021 English set A (set code NYRG-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the most appropriate word or group of words for the blank.

He dislikes ______ punish his friends.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Choose the word that fits grammar and meaning.
Step 1: 'Dislikes having to' takes the gerund after 'dislike'.
Answer: (b).
questions.source: CDS II 2021 English set A (set code NYRG-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Vocabulary
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the underlined word.

He __drowned__ in the flood water last year.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Synonym.
Step 1: 'Drowned' means went under water. 'Submerged' is the nearest.
Answer: (c).
questions.source: CDS II 2021 English set A (set code NYRG-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Vocabulary
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the underlined word.

Autumn is rather a __dry__ season.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Synonym.
Step 1: 'Dry' means without moisture. 'Arid' is the nearest.
Answer: (a).
questions.source: CDS II 2021 English set A (set code NYRG-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Vocabulary
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the underlined word.

Our __differences__ are growing day by day.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Synonym.
Step 1: 'Differences' here means conflicts, so 'disagreements'.
Answer: (c).
questions.source: CDS II 2021 English set A (set code NYRG-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Vocabulary
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the underlined word.

The big tree __hindered__ access of sunlight into the house.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Synonym.
Step 1: 'Hindered' means obstructed. 'Impeded' is the nearest.
Answer: (a).
questions.source: CDS II 2021 English set A (set code NYRG-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Vocabulary
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the underlined word.

The __complexity__ of the issue baffled everyone.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Synonym.
Step 1: 'Complexity' means the quality of being complicated. 'Intricacy' is the nearest.
Answer: (b).
questions.source: CDS II 2021 English set A (set code NYRG-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Vocabulary
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the underlined word.

He drank __excessive__ amount of liquor.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Synonym.
Step 1: 'Excessive' means beyond what is normal. 'Inordinate' is the nearest.
Step 2: 'Unreasonable' is related, but 'inordinate' is the closer word for quantity.
Answer: (b).
questions.source: CDS II 2021 English set A (set code NYRG-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Vocabulary
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the underlined word.

He __initiated__ the dialogue.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Synonym.
Step 1: 'Initiated' means started. 'Began' is the nearest.
Answer: (c).
questions.source: CDS II 2021 English set A (set code NYRG-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Vocabulary
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the underlined word.

She looked __pale__ after recovering from Covid-19.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Synonym.
Step 1: 'Pale' means lacking colour. 'Sallow' means a sickly pale yellow.
Step 2: 'Ruddy', 'glowing' and 'radiant' mean the opposite.
Answer: (a).
questions.source: CDS II 2021 English set A (set code NYRG-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Vocabulary
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the underlined word.

I __overrule__ your proposal.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Synonym.
Step 1: To overrule a proposal is to reject it by authority. 'Veto' is the nearest.
Answer: (b).
questions.source: CDS II 2021 English set A (set code NYRG-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Vocabulary
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the underlined word.

His behaviour __shocked__ me.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Synonym.
Step 1: 'Shocked' means deeply disturbed. 'Appalled' is the nearest.
Answer: (c).
questions.source: CDS II 2021 English set A (set code NYRG-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Vocabulary
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the option opposite in meaning to the underlined word.

I am very __particular__ about it.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Antonym.
Step 1: 'Particular' means exact and careful. The opposite is 'vague'.
Step 2: 'Precise' is a synonym.
Answer: (b).
questions.source: CDS II 2021 English set A (set code NYRG-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Vocabulary
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the option opposite in meaning to the underlined word.

He has become __paunchy__.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Antonym.
Step 1: 'Paunchy' means having a big belly. The opposite is 'slim'.
Answer: (b).
questions.source: CDS II 2021 English set A (set code NYRG-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Vocabulary
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the option opposite in meaning to the underlined word.

This river __originates__ from the Ganges.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Antonym.
Step 1: 'Originates' means begins. The opposite is 'culminates' (reaches an end).
Answer: (b).
questions.source: CDS II 2021 English set A (set code NYRG-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Vocabulary
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the option opposite in meaning to the underlined word.

The film I saw was __hilarious__.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Antonym.
Step 1: 'Hilarious' means very funny. The opposite is 'serious'.
Step 2: 'Tragic' fits less well, since it means sad rather than not funny.
Answer: (b).
questions.source: CDS II 2021 English set A (set code NYRG-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Vocabulary
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the option opposite in meaning to the underlined word.

On that day, __pandemonium__ reigned in the hall.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Antonym.
Step 1: 'Pandemonium' means wild noise and disorder. The opposite is 'peace'.
Answer: (c).
questions.source: CDS II 2021 English set A (set code NYRG-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Vocabulary
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the option opposite in meaning to the underlined word.

The police __detained__ me today amidst busy traffic.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Antonym.
Step 1: 'Detained' means held in custody. The opposite is 'released'.
Answer: (b).
questions.source: CDS II 2021 English set A (set code NYRG-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Vocabulary
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the option opposite in meaning to the underlined word.

In my state of __despair__, I confessed everything.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Antonym.
Step 1: 'Despair' means loss of hope. The opposite is 'elation' (great joy).
Step 2: 'Determination' is not the opposite: it is firmness, not joy.
Answer: (d).
questions.source: CDS II 2021 English set A (set code NYRG-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Vocabulary
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the option opposite in meaning to the underlined word.

He was __accused__ by the entire community after he failed in the mission.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Antonym.
Step 1: 'Accused' means blamed. The opposite is 'vindicated' (cleared of blame).
Answer: (a).
questions.source: CDS II 2021 English set A (set code NYRG-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Vocabulary
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the option opposite in meaning to the underlined word.

There was much to __boast__ about the quality of his work.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Antonym.
Step 1: 'Boast' means to speak proudly. The opposite is 'deprecate' (to belittle).
Answer: (c).
questions.source: CDS II 2021 English set A (set code NYRG-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Vocabulary
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the option opposite in meaning to the underlined word.

He delivered an __eccentric__ speech.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Antonym.
Step 1: 'Eccentric' means unusual. The opposite is 'a normal' speech.
Answer: (c).
questions.source: CDS II 2021 English set A (set code NYRG-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Find which part of speech the underlined word or phrase belongs to.

They wandered __around__ aimlessly.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Part of speech depends on the job a word does in the sentence.
Step 1: 'Around' tells where they wandered, with no object after it, so it is an adverb.
Answer: (c).

Note: This question has been lightly edited from the printed paper for clarity and a single defensible answer.
questions.source: CDS II 2021 English set A (set code NYRG-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Find which part of speech the underlined word or phrase belongs to.

We went away __after__ they had left.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Part of speech depends on the job a word does in the sentence.
Step 1: 'After' introduces the clause 'they had left', so it is a conjunction.
Answer: (d).
questions.source: CDS II 2021 English set A (set code NYRG-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Find which part of speech the underlined word or phrase belongs to.

Public culture is associated with __extremely new__ civil societies.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Part of speech depends on the job a word does in the sentence.
Step 1: 'Extremely' strengthens the adjective 'new', so it is an intensifier.
Step 2: The whole underlined phrase works as an adjective phrase, so treat this item as low-confidence.
Answer: (b).
questions.source: CDS II 2021 English set A (set code NYRG-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Find which part of speech the underlined word or phrase belongs to.

You are paying __less__ attention to your studies these days.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Part of speech depends on the job a word does in the sentence.
Step 1: 'Less' describes the amount of attention, so it works as an adjective (determiner).
Answer: (b).
questions.source: CDS II 2021 English set A (set code NYRG-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Find which part of speech the underlined word or phrase belongs to.

__Why__, is it really Sujata on the phone?
questions.explanation:
Concept: Part of speech depends on the job a word does in the sentence.
Step 1: 'Why' at the start of a sentence expresses surprise, so it is an interjection.
Answer: (a).
questions.source: CDS II 2021 English set A (set code NYRG-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Find which part of speech the underlined word or phrase belongs to.

Sit down and rest a __while__.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Part of speech depends on the job a word does in the sentence.
Step 1: 'A while' names a period of time, so 'while' is a noun.
Answer: (d).
questions.source: CDS II 2021 English set A (set code NYRG-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Find which part of speech the underlined word or phrase belongs to.

Rakesh is __too__ old to run fast.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Part of speech depends on the job a word does in the sentence.
Step 1: 'Too' modifies the adjective 'old', so it is an adverb of degree.
Step 2: (c) 'Intensifier' is also defensible, so treat this item as low-confidence.
Answer: (a).
questions.source: CDS II 2021 English set A (set code NYRG-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Find which part of speech the underlined word or phrase belongs to.

For the next generation of interior architects and design graduates, work __opportunities__ are immense.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Part of speech depends on the job a word does in the sentence.
Step 1: 'Opportunities' is the subject of the sentence, so it is a noun.
Answer: (c).
questions.source: CDS II 2021 English set A (set code NYRG-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Find which part of speech the underlined word or phrase belongs to.

Life is a __solo__ fight, and each person makes his or her own journey.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Part of speech depends on the job a word does in the sentence.
Step 1: 'Solo' describes the noun 'fight', so it is an adjective.
Answer: (b).
questions.source: CDS II 2021 English set A (set code NYRG-F-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Find which part of speech the underlined word or phrase belongs to.

__The__ cat loves comfort.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Part of speech depends on the job a word does in the sentence.
